tool.name: mhcquant IonAnnotator
tool.description: Annotate MS2 spectra with theoretical fragment ions of FDR-filtered peptides

param.name: spectra
param.label: Replicate mzML files of one sample
param.help: The mzML files of the sample, in the same order as they were merged by IDMerger

param.name: idxml
param.label: FDR-filtered idXML
param.help: Contains the final peptide identifications of the sample (one hit per peptide identification)

param.label: Precursor charge range
param.help: Minimum:maximum precursor charge, e.g. 2:3. Only the minimum of the range is used: fragment ion charges are derived from the precursor charge of each peptide hit (hit charge minus one, at least 1)

param.label: Fragment mass tolerance (Da)
param.help: Tolerance used for matching theoretical and experimental fragment ions

param.label: Add a-ions
param.help: Include a-ions in the theoretical spectrum generation

param.label: Add c-ions
param.help: Include c-ions in the theoretical spectrum generation

param.label: Add x-ions
param.help: Include x-ions in the theoretical spectrum generation

param.label: Add z-ions
param.help: Include z-ions in the theoretical spectrum generation

tool.help:
**What it does**
Annotates DDA MS2 spectra with the theoretical fragment ions of the FDR-filtered peptide identifications, in the spirit of the `get_ion_annotations.py` helper shipped with the nf-core/mhcquant pipeline. b- and y-ions are always considered; a-, c-, x- and z-ions can be added optionally.
For every peak of every MS2 spectrum referenced by the filtered idXML, the tool reports the observed m/z and intensity and whether the peak matches (within the given fragment mass tolerance) a theoretical fragment ion of the assigned peptide sequence. This aids the manual validation of peptide-spectrum matches, a common step in immunopeptidomics workflows such as MHC ligand identification.
-----
**Inputs**
- **Replicate mzML files of one sample**: the MS2 spectra of the sample. Provide all replicate mzML files that were merged into the idXML by IDMerger, **in the same order as they were passed to IDMerger** (peptide identifications are matched to the mzML files by their position). - **FDR-filtered idXML**: the final peptide identifications of the sample, e.g. the output of OpenMS IDFilter at the desired peptide-level FDR. Each peptide identification must contain a single peptide hit. The idXML must have been created by OpenMS IDMerger with `annotate_file_origin` enabled (the default in the Galaxy IDMerger wrapper) so that peptide identifications can be assigned to their source mzML files.
-----
**Outputs**
- **Matching ions** (`*_matching_ions.tsv`): all observed peaks that match a theoretical fragment ion of the peptide (peptide sequence, ion name, ion charge, theoretical and experimental m/z, intensity, and the corresponding peak ID in the all peaks table). Only reported when at least two matching ions were found for a spectrum. - **All peaks** (`*_all_peaks.tsv`): all peaks of the referenced MS2 spectra with their peptide assignment, m/z, intensity, whether they are a matching ion, the spectrum native ID, and the name of their source mzML file as recorded in the idXML.
-----
**Options**
- **Precursor charge range**: minimum:maximum precursor charge, e.g. `2:3`. Only the minimum of the range is used; the fragment ion charges are derived from the precursor charge stored in the idXML (hit charge minus one, at least 1). - **Fragment mass tolerance (Da)**: absolute tolerance for matching theoretical and experimental fragment ions (default 0.02 Da). - **Add a-, c-, x-, z-ions**: extend the theoretical spectrum beyond the default b/y series.
-----
**Credits**
This tool wraps `get_ion_annotations.py`, written by Jonas Scheid (MIT license) for the nf-core/mhcquant pipeline: https://github.com/nf-core/mhcquant
If you use this tool in your research, please cite MHCquant:
- MHCquant2 refines immunopeptidomics tumor antigen discovery. Genome Biology 26:290 (2025). doi: `10.1186/s13059-025-03763-8`
